summary.profileStatement: I'm a security infrastructure and automation engineer who documents why each decision was made, a habit built through license reviews and audit-defense work. The same principle carried me from KAI's closed-network OA operations through FSDC and Financial Supervisory Service audits, then Nextrade's build phase and the Korean Financial Services Commission main-license review, into the current automation phase. FortiGate HA and network segmentation, Splunk ES detection rules, Slack/SMS notifications, FortiManager API lookups, and Claude AI-assisted review now form one response architecture that cuts down the console-hopping an operator used to do. en.headline: An engineer who designs explainable security automation
paragraphs: My career started inside Korea Aerospace Industries' closed network, tracking patch schedules for the closed-network Linux fleet on an Excel sheet. The repetition drove one conviction: security engineering is not about hoping incidents never happen, it is about lowering risk through repeatable procedures, automation, and documentation. RHCSA, LPIC-1, and Linux Master Level 2 came next, rebuilding the Linux foundation, and that base carried directly into hands-on automation work.

At Metanet M Platform I picked up Ansible and Python, and turned the NAC policy deployment procedure into a single reviewable workflow for contact-center operations. At Jointree, NSX-T microsegmentation on Kookmin University's next-generation information system closed the east-west traffic blind spots, and the NAC and DLP detection policies got the same reviewable treatment. The tools changed, but the principle held: any task that takes repeated manual effort is a candidate for a runbook.

At Quantec Investment Management's Financial Security Data Center (FSDC), the Financial Supervisory Service audits taught a different lesson: security infrastructure is not a one-time setup, it is the ability to present current state and change history with data during audits and incidents. Tuning DB access-control queries and validating the PB platform POC were both acts of explaining system state with data and leaving an auditable trail for changes.

Most recently, in the Nextrade exchange security track, the engagement ran continuously from the build phase at Gaonnuri through the automation phase at ITCEN CTS. Network segmentation and endpoint security controls went up first, with the Korean Financial Services Commission main-license review on the critical path. I pulled Splunk ES detection rules, the alert workflow, FortiManager API policy lookups, and Claude AI-assisted review into one operating setup, so a detected event carried straight through to alert delivery.

Next, I am widening the scope of automation tooling from security appliances and scripts toward MCP and Edge runtimes. The homelab (Cloudflare Workers, MCP, Grafana, 1Password) runs on Terraform-managed IaC, where the experiment is letting an MCP tool take the first pass over repetitive security-response items. In the next chapter, I want the security problem to come before the tool, and to take on the role of turning that problem into a repeatable engineering structure.
en.closing: I will work with you to frame the next problem your security infrastructure needs to solve, by reducing repeated work and leaving an operating record behind.
